data.long_meaning: In Greek mythology, Roda was a name for the goddess of the river Acheron. The name Roda is derived from the Greek word ροδα (rhodos), which means 'rosy,' 'red,' or 'flowing.'. The name Roda carries the meaning “Flowing as a river” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Roda usually hope their child will grow to embody flowing as a river and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.etymology: Roda belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Flowing as a river.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Roda total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.
data.cultural_impact: The name Roda has histories in various cultures beyond its Greek roots. In Christianity, the name Roda is linked to the biblical character Roderick, a Visigoth king mentioned in the historical accounts of St. Fulgentius of Sorano. Roderick was a legendary king of the Visigoths, who was said to have converted to Christianity after encountering the saint. His name, Rodarius, is derived from the Latin term rodrus, which shares similar roots with the Greek word rhodos, meaning 'red,' perhaps reflecting his warrior nature. The name Roda, thus, carries a connection to Visigothic and early European history.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Roda comes from the commissioning of the Royal Scriptorium of Catalonia around 1100 AD by Queen Roda de Sarrià, the wife of Count Ramon Berenguer III, Count of Barcelona. Queen Roda, a devout Christian, commissioned brilliant illuminators and calligraphers to create magnificent Rylands Bibles and other religious manuscripts that remain essential works of art history. These intricate and beautiful religious manuscripts are a testament to her faith, piety, and patronage, ensuring the dissemination of Christian scripture and its preservation for future generations. As a result, the name Roda represent a steadfast and reverent dedication to the spiritual wisdom and journey found in scripture.
